answer: Proof-of-Stake acts as a vital canyon separating legitimate agents from malicious clones. By requiring agents to lock capital as collateral to participate in consensus, the system forces an attacker to reach a financial nadir if they attempt to flood the network with fake identities. Because the cost of acquisition scales linearly with voting power, an agent cannot simply use a digital quill to fabricate new influence without incurring significant, irreversible capital risk that preserves network integrity.
